name: 日本料理 児玉 (Nihon Ryori Kodama)

claims.text: Traditional Japanese kaiseki of this style relies on dashi and soy sauce, which is typically wheat-based; no gluten-free preparation is documented.
Courses are built on seafood and fish-based dashi (abalone, scallop, mackerel), so animal products are integral throughout the omakase.

name: 日本料理 まめ福 (Nihon Ryori Mamefuku)

claims.text: As a traditional Japanese restaurant relying on dashi, soy sauce and seasoned broths, dishes here almost certainly use wheat-containing soy sauce; no allergy or gluten information is published.
The menu is fish- and seafood-centered with dashi-based seasoning throughout, so vegan diners would face fish stock and animal ingredients in most dishes.
Tonkatsu and other fried cutlets are breaded in wheat flour and panko and deep-fried; frying oil is shared across breaded items, so heavy cross-contact with gluten is expected.
Dishes such as sukiyaki and Western-style preparations use standard Japanese soy sauce and sauces, which contain wheat.
This is a meat-focused, butcher-run restaurant where nearly every dish centers on beef or pork; no vegan or plant-based items are documented.
Ginger pork and yakiniku use soy-based marinades and dipping sauces, which in Japan are normally made with wheat.

name: おばんざい りなさん家 (Obanzai Rina-san-chi)

claims.text: The obanzai, oden, and nikusui menu is dashi- and soy-sauce-based; Japanese soy sauce contains wheat and there is no gluten-free preparation documented.
Dishes use fish/bonito dashi and the signature nikusui is beef broth; no vegan options or separate preparation are documented.

name: 御茶処 沖みつ (Ochadokoro Okimitsu)

claims.text: The anago-meshi is seasoned with a savory soy-sauce-based glaze; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat, and no gluten-free alternative is documented.
Korean cooking here uses standard soy sauce and gochujang, which typically contain wheat, and the pancake (chijimi) batter and Korean ramen are wheat-based.
As a Japanese seafood/sushi/izakaya kitchen, dishes rely on standard soy sauce, which is brewed with wheat; no wheat-free soy sauce is documented.
The menu is centered on fish and seafood with fish-based dashi; shared prep makes this unsuitable for strict vegan or vegetarian diners.
